description: We are ASTRONUM, a team united by our passion for science, technology, and the mysteries of the universe, with the purpose of sharing the fascinating adventure of space exploration with other young people.
summary: Astronum is an interactive educational website, designed for people aged 12 to 30, that remembers the equipment humanity has left behind in space. Landers on the Moon, rovers on Mars and probes drifting through deep space may have gone silent, but their story is still worth telling. The site brings together 22 of these missions (8 to the Moon, 8 to Mars and 6 to deep space), from Ranger and Apollo to Perseverance, Voyager and New Horizons.
details:
Astronum is an educational digital atlas focused on the artifacts humanity has left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Visitors can choose one of three destinations and explore 22 NASA space missions. For each mission, users can discover its history, the equipment involved, how it functioned, and what it uncovered. Each destination concludes with a “Mission Completed!” screen featuring an animated video. The experience includes voice narration and is available in both Spanish and English.

Technology Stack

  • HTML5, CSS3, and vanilla JavaScript, with no frameworks, all in a single file.
  • Voice narration using the browser's Web Speech API, with online audio as a fallback.
  • Sound effects using the Web Audio API and an animated starfield background rendered with Canvas.
  • MP4 videos and animated WebP images embedded directly into the file.
  • Responsive design for mobile devices (styles for screens up to 600 px) and support for the "reduced motion" accessibility preference.
  • ES/EN language selector with the preference saved in the browser.
  • Google Fonts: Poppins.

Innovation Highlights

  • Narrative Design: A journey through three destinations, culminating in a completed mission.
  • Educational Value: Each mission explains what the spacecraft was, how it worked, what it accomplished, and what happened to it, along with a glossary of terms.
  • Visual Simplicity: Galaxy background, clear typography, and high contrast.
  • Accessibility: Text synchronized with voice narration, options to pause or mute narration, and bilingual audio.
  • Data Reliability: Recommended NASA sources and APA-formatted image credits for each mission. It is worth clarifying that 12 of the 22 images cite third-party websites (media outlets, Wikimedia, and ESA), so I would not claim that they all come from NASA. The website footer already identifies this as an independent educational project.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

  • ChatGPT: Website programming and development.
  • Claude (Anthropic): Website improvements, including the integration of mission-ending videos, welcome audio in Spanish and English, and the review of links and sources.
  • Canva: Creation of animated images.
  • CapCut: Creation of the project presentation video.
